newsitem.title: UK: UK heart expert says fruit, veg better than pills.
newsitem.headline: UK heart expert says fruit, veg better than pills.

text.p: Eating fruit and vegetables is far better than taking vitamins if you want to prevent a heart attack, a British heart specialist said on Tuesday.

Dr Andrew Ness of Addenbrookes hospital in Cambridge told a conference on cardiovascular disease prevention that taking Vitamin C, Vitamin E and Beta-carotene vitamin pills was no substitute for eating fresh fruit and vegetables.
"There is no conclusive evidence that taking any of these vitamin supplements reduces the risk of cardiovascular disease," Ness said.
"As things stand we should not be recommending this. Rather we should be recommending that people eat a diet rich in fruit and vegetables.
"I think it is true that people could be wasting their money...My concern is that in taking single vitamin supplements, people may be wasting money and be given a false sense of security," Ness said.
Ness drew his conclusions after reviewing international studies in which people suffering from heart disease were given supplements of Vitamin C, or Vitamin E or betacarotene.
Dr Neil Poulter shared Ness's concern that some people might take vitamin pills as an insurance policy against heart disease without changing their diet or taking more exercise.
"I think there is a danger of substituting these expensive products for things that we know are effective," Poulter said.
